rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should test a multimodal baseline to evaluate if combining RNA and image data improves performance. This clarifies the potential value of multimodal approaches, which are central to the study. Testing a simple concatenation fusion with standard encoders (PCA for RNA, ResNet50 for images) isolates the effect of modality combination without overcomplicating other factors.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion) achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. Since fusion is a critical design choice in multimodal models, this comparison directly addresses uncertainty about its impact while building on the previous multimodal setup.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with concat fusion (0.5265) slightly outperform weighted fusion (0.5232). This experiment tests the impact of multiprofile settings and avgpool aggregation, which are unexplored in previous multimodal configurations. By keeping RNA/image encoders consistent and only changing profile and aggregation, it isolates the effect of these key design choices while building on prior multimodal success.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_018) achieve high validation accuracy (0.618). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (config_019) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion method while keeping other parameters constant. It balances exploitation of the promising multiprofile setup with exploration of fusion strategies.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_019, 0.639 accuracy) are strongest. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with a more powerful imagenet_vit_l image encoder and switching to transformer aggregation, which could improve performance. It isolates the effect of these two critical design choices (image encoder and aggregation) while maintaining the high-performing multiprofile and weighted fusion setup, balancing exploration and exploitation.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50, using avgpool and weighted fusion, achieve high accuracy (0.638999). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l and switching aggregation to transformer, which could improve performance by leveraging a more powerful image encoder and dynamic aggregation. This clarifies the impact of image encoder quality and aggregation method, balancing exploration of key components while building on the promising multiprofile foundation.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile setups with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with concat fusion, exploring whether a different aggregation method could further improve performance. It balances exploration of aggregation techniques with the promising multiprofile setup, avoiding redundant changes while addressing key design uncertainty.

The existing evidence shows that config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scvi_n200 while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. This is a critical exploration since RNA encoding is a key component, and scvi_n200 may offer better representation. It balances exploitation (building on the successful multiprofile/weighted setup) and exploration (testing a new encoder).

The existing evidence shows that rna_only models with scvi_n200 encoder and multiprofile setting (config_031) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests a multimodal setup with scgpt RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder, using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. It clarifies whether combining modalities with advanced encoders can surpass the current best, addressing the uncertainty about the potential of complex models. This is the best use of the final experiment to explore high-impact design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_039) achieve high accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder, aggregation, and fusion settings to isolate the impact of RNA encoder quality. Since scgpt is a more advanced encoder than scvi_n200, this comparison could reveal if it outperforms the current best, directly addressing the key design choice of RNA representation.
